html:
Lan Xang, the Kingdom of a Million Elephants, was founded in 1353 by Fa Ngum, who united the Lao lands along the Mekong with Khmer support. Its first capital was at today's Luang Prabang.

Fa Ngum had grown up at the Khmer court, and he brought Theravada Buddhism and a revered image, the Phra Bang, from Cambodia. Lan Xang grew into one of the largest states in Southeast Asia, rival to Ayutthaya, Lan Na and Vietnam.

It reached its height under Setthathirath in the 16th century and under Sourigna Vongsa in the 17th, then split apart in 1707 (see kingdom of Luang Phrabang). Lao people still look to it as the founding state of their nation.
